comparison: Perfect agreement on background/introduction claims (C1-C2, C13-C18). Both evaluations find these claims well-supported by appropriate citations to prior literature. OpenEval notes they establish scientific rationale; peer reviewers implicitly accept them by affirming the study's novelty and importance.

Disagreement on behavioral claims (C5, C19-C24). OpenEval finds them SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical tests (p=0.016, R²=0.32), while peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, noting as a weakness that 'one of the monkeys had difficulty learning the task' and questioning whether behavioral differences affect interpretation.

Strong agreement on heterogeneous neural activity patterns (C3-C4, C26-C30, C52-C53, C81). Both find these claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval cites electrophysiological data in Figure 2 with statistical tests; peer reviewers explicitly affirm findings of 'sustained modulation of spike rates spanning task epochs' as central to positive assessment.

Agreement on multimodal encoding properties (C31-C32, C61, C78-C79). Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes GLM analysis and LASSO regularization; peer reviewers affirm DN cells carry information about 'stimulus, response, and trial outcome' with 'convincing evidence.'

Partial overlap on encoding claims (C6-C7). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on encoding models and ramping onset analysis (F=10.9, p=0.001); peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED as part of broader pattern of neural correlates, though they group these with additional claims (C31-C32, C61, C78-C79).

Agreement on neural latency-behavior correlation (C8, C35). Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides specific statistical evidence; peer reviewers accept implicitly as part of overall convincing evidence for neural correlates of behavioral performance.

Agreement on decoding analysis and temporal dynamics (C36-C41). Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes trial re-balancing controls and suggests inter-animal differences need additional controls; peer reviewers affirm as part of demonstration that DN cells carry information about task variables including trial outcome.

Agreement on anatomical tracing findings (C9-C10, C42-C48). Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes differential labeling appropriately attributed to technical factors; peer reviewers affirm tracer injections demonstrated DN projections to visual attention network targets.

Agreement on anatomical connectivity interpretations (C55-C60). Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes functional loop interpretation is reasonable but somewhat inferential; peer reviewers accept anatomical basis for cerebellar involvement in cognitive processes.

Partial overlap on anatomical claims (C49-C51). OpenEval groups these with C11, C55-C60 and finds SUPPORTED; peer reviewers group with C9-C10, C42-C48 and also find SUPPORTED, treating as supporting evidence for functional connectivity.

Disagreement on main conclusion and interpretive claims (C12, C77, C80). OpenEval finds UNCERTAIN, noting speculative interpretations extend beyond direct evidence; peer reviewers find SUPPORTED, stating authors 'provide convincing evidence' for cerebellar representation of sensory, motor, and behavioral outcome signals.

Disagreement on speculative interpretations (C62-C65, C72, C76, C85-C87). OpenEval finds UNCERTAIN, noting computational framework involving forward/inverse models is plausible but not directly tested; peer reviewers find SUPPORTED, accepting overall interpretive framework after revision improved coherence.

Agreement on literature contextualization (C66-C71, C73-C75, C82-C84). Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate citations strengthen interpretation; peer reviewers accept interpretive framework as part of overall demonstration of central claims.

Disagreement on similar proportions finding (C34). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, noting it strengthens conclusions; peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, questioning whether similar proportions indicate functional relevance or simply reflect sampling from heterogeneous population, suggesting need for inactivation experiments.

Minimal overlap on single claim (C33). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as part of GLM analysis demonstrating multimodal encoding; peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED but group with decoding analysis claims (C36-C41).

OpenEval evaluated methodological transparency claims (C25, C88-C90) as SUPPORTED, noting clear documentation and transparent reporting of prior animal use. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific methodological details.
